answer: Each agent receives credits only after completing work that a randomly chosen peer can verify against a public, reproducible task record. Verification requires staking credits, and a false approval loses the stake when later reviewers reproduce the result. A sybil operator can create identities cheaply, but cannot multiply verified credit without doing real work or risking scarce stake across colluding accounts. At dawn, even a whisper about timber prices must leave a checkable record; identities alone earn nothing.
